atoms.name: bit_and
atoms.rule: a ∧ b is bitwise AND on nonnegative integers.
atoms.plain: a ∧ b is bitwise AND on nonnegative integers.

atoms.name: bit_or
atoms.rule: a ∨ b is bitwise OR on nonnegative integers.
atoms.plain: a ∨ b is bitwise OR on nonnegative integers.

atoms.name: bit_xor
atoms.rule: a ⊻ b is bitwise XOR on nonnegative integers.
atoms.plain: a ⊻ b is bitwise XOR on nonnegative integers.

atoms.name: shift_left
atoms.rule: a ⇐ b shifts nonnegative a left by b bits; counts above 31 give NaN.
atoms.plain: a ⇐ b shifts nonnegative a left by b bits; counts above 31 give NaN.

atoms.name: shift_right
atoms.rule: a ⇒ b shifts nonnegative a right by b bits.
atoms.plain: a ⇒ b shifts nonnegative a right by b bits.

atoms.name: bit_count
atoms.rule: a ♯ counts the one bits of nonnegative a; negative inputs give NaN.
atoms.plain: a ♯ counts the one bits of nonnegative a; negative inputs give NaN.

domain.en: Values are nonnegative integers read as bit patterns; the lamps show the lowest eight bits.

settings.en: The preset that selects these atoms and defaults.
A recursive call unfolds at most this many times; larger counters give NaN.
The range of numbers in generated expressions and branch thresholds.

why.en: These atoms are one example. Atoms are chosen by the user: any function with a rule can be registered and the same three composition forms grow operators from it.

operators.name: □₁
operators.definition: a □₁ = { a ∧ a }
operators.plain: AND a with a bit by bit.

operators.name: ★₂
operators.definition: a ★₂ b = { (2 ●₁₀) ▼₁₉ a, if a < 29 and b >= 9 and b < 15; b, else }
operators.plain: If a < 29 and b ≥ 9 and b < 15, apply ●₁₀ to 2, then apply ▼₁₉ to the result and a; otherwise return b.

operators.name: ♧₃
operators.definition: ♧₃ a = { a, if a == 0; a ∨ (♧₃ (a ⇒ 1)), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is a; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then replace r by a ∨ r.

operators.name: ▽₄
operators.plain: Apply □₁ to 16, then XOR it with a bit by bit.

operators.name: ♡₅
operators.plain: Shift a right by the number of one bits in a bits.

operators.name: ♣₆
operators.plain: Apply ♡₅ to a, then shift the result left by itself bits.

operators.name: ◆₇
operators.definition: a ◆₇ b = { ♡₅ (a ⇒ b) }
operators.plain: Shift a right by b bits, then apply ♡₅ to the result.

operators.name: ▽₈
operators.plain: Count the one bits of a, then shift it left by ♡₅ 2 bits.

operators.name: ★₉
operators.plain: Apply ♡₅ to a, then shift it right by b ♣₆ bits.

operators.name: ●₁₀
operators.definition: a ●₁₀ = { (a ⇐ a) □₁ }
operators.plain: Shift a left by a bits, then apply □₁ to the result.

operators.name: ☆₁₁
operators.plain: Apply ♣₆ to a, then apply ★₉ to the result and (♡₅ 0).

operators.name: ◆₁₂
operators.definition: ◆₁₂ a = { (a ♣₆) ∨ (a ●₁₀) }
operators.plain: Apply ♣₆ to a, then OR it with a ●₁₀ bit by bit.

operators.name: □₁₃
operators.definition: □₁₃ a = { (♡₅ a) ⊻ a }
operators.plain: Apply ♡₅ to a, then XOR it with a bit by bit.

operators.name: ◇₁₄
operators.definition: a ◇₁₄ b = { (b ★₉ a) ▽₈ }
operators.plain: Apply ★₉ to b and a, then apply ▽₈ to the result.

operators.name: ■₁₅
operators.definition: ■₁₅ a = { a ⇒ (a ♣₆) }
operators.plain: Shift a right by a ♣₆ bits.

operators.name: ■₁₆
operators.plain: XOR 19 with a bit by bit, then apply ☆₁₁ to the result.

operators.name: ▲₁₇
operators.definition: ▲₁₇ a = { ♡₅ (a ⇐ a) }
operators.plain: Shift a left by a bits, then apply ♡₅ to the result.

operators.name: ♠₁₈
operators.definition: ♠₁₈ a = { (■₁₅ a) ⊻ a }
operators.plain: Apply ■₁₅ to a, then XOR it with a bit by bit.

operators.name: ▼₁₉
operators.definition: a ▼₁₉ b = { (a ★₉ b) ▽₈, if a >= 17 and b >= 30; □₁₃ (7 ◇₁₄ b), if a >= 17 and b >= 29 and b < 30; (□₁₃ a) ◆₇ (▲₁₇ b), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 17 and b ≥ 30, apply ★₉ to a and b, then apply ▽₈ to the result; otherwise if a ≥ 17 and b ≥ 29 and b < 30, apply ◇₁₄ to 7 and b, then apply □₁₃ to the result; otherwise apply □₁₃ to a, then apply ◆₇ to the result and (▲₁₇ b).

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ♤₂₀
operators.definition: a ♤₂₀ b = { b ⇒ a, if a >= 26 and b < 0; a ♯, if a < 10 and b >= 0 and b < 6; ☆₁₁ a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 26 and b < 0, shift b right by a bits; otherwise if a < 10 and b ≥ 0 and b < 6, count the one bits of a; otherwise apply ☆₁₁ to a.

operators.name: ♦₂₁
operators.definition: a ♦₂₁ b = { □₁₃ (a ★₉ 15), if a >= 1 and a < 8 and b < 23; ☆₁₁ (1 ♤₂₀ a), if a < 1 and b < 23; (b ⇒ a) ■₁₆, else }
operators.plain: If 1 ≤ a < 8 and b < 23, apply ★₉ to a and 15, then apply □₁₃ to the result; otherwise if a < 1 and b < 23, apply ♤₂₀ to 1 and a, then apply ☆₁₁ to the result; otherwise shift b right by a bits, then apply ■₁₆ to the result.

operators.name: △₂₂
operators.definition: a △₂₂ b = { 0 ▽₈, if a < 2 and b < 17; a ▽₈, if a >= 12 and a < 20 and b < 17; b ∧ 18, else }
operators.plain: If a < 2 and b < 17, apply ▽₈ to 0; otherwise if 12 ≤ a < 20 and b < 17, apply ▽₈ to a; otherwise AND b with 18 bit by bit.

operators.name: ▽₂₃
operators.definition: ▽₂₃ a = { (♡₅ a) ∨ (a ▽₄), if a >= 6 and a < 9; (☆₁₁ a) ▼₁₉ (a ▽₄), if a >= 11; (☆₁₁ a) ⇒ (☆₁₁ a), else }
operators.plain: If 6 ≤ a < 9, apply ♡₅ to a, then OR it with a ▽₄ bit by bit; otherwise if a ≥ 11, apply ☆₁₁ to a, then apply ▼₁₉ to the result and (a ▽₄); otherwise apply ☆₁₁ to a, then shift the result right by itself bits.

operators.name: ♤₂₄
operators.definition: ♤₂₄ a = { (▽₂₃ a) ∨ (▲₁₇ a), if a >= 10 and a < 15; ■₁₅ (▽₂₃ a), if a >= 1 and a < 10; (a ◆₇ a) ♣₆, else }
operators.plain: If 10 ≤ a < 15, apply ▽₂₃ to a, then OR it with ▲₁₇ a bit by bit; otherwise if 1 ≤ a < 10, apply ▽₂₃ to a, then apply ■₁₅ to the result; otherwise apply ◆₇ to a and a, then apply ♣₆ to the result.

operators.name: ●₂₅
operators.definition: a ●₂₅ b = { (▽₂₃ b) ★₂ (a ♣₆), if a < 2 and b >= 6 and b < 9; (▲₁₇ b) ★₂ (◆₁₂ a), else }
operators.plain: If a < 2 and b ≥ 6 and b < 9, apply ▽₂₃ to b, then apply ★₂ to the result and (a ♣₆); otherwise apply ▲₁₇ to b, then apply ★₂ to the result and (◆₁₂ a).

operators.name: △₂₆
operators.definition: a △₂₆ b = { ♤₂₄ b, if a < 11 and b >= 23; b ♤₂₀ b, else }
operators.plain: If a < 11 and b ≥ 23, apply ♤₂₄ to b; otherwise compute b ♤₂₀ b.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ■₂₇
operators.definition: a ■₂₇ b = { (□₁₃ a) ∨ (b ▽₈), if a >= 1 and a < 12 and b >= 23; (☆₁₁ a) △₂₆ 3, else }
operators.plain: If 1 ≤ a < 12 and b ≥ 23, apply □₁₃ to a, then OR it with b ▽₈ bit by bit; otherwise apply ☆₁₁ to a, then apply △₂₆ to the result and 3.

operators.name: ♥₂₈
operators.definition: a ♥₂₈ b = { (♤₂₄ a) ♦₂₁ (b ■₁₆), if a >= 10 and a < 18 and b >= 12; (5 ■₁₆) ⇒ (a ♯), if a >= 18 and b >= 2 and b < 12; (b ■₁₆) ■₂₇ (b ♣₆), else }
operators.plain: Chooses between 3 cases by testing a and b; the cases combine ■₁₆, ■₂₇, ♣₆, ♤₂₄, ♦₂₁, ⇒ and ♯.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ♥₂₉
operators.definition: a ♥₂₉ = { (a ∧ a) ●₁₀, if a >= 3 and a < 13; a, if a < 3; (♠₁₈ a) ■₂₇ (16 ●₁₀), else }
operators.plain: If 3 ≤ a < 13, AND a with a bit by bit, then apply ●₁₀ to the result; otherwise if a < 3, return a; otherwise apply ♠₁₈ to a, then apply ■₂₇ to the result and (16 ●₁₀).

operators.name: ♥₃₀
operators.definition: a ♥₃₀ = { (◆₁₂ a) ∨ a }
operators.plain: Apply ◆₁₂ to a, then OR it with a bit by bit.

operators.name: ■₃₁
operators.definition: a ■₃₁ b = { (12 ♥₃₀) ∧ (▽₂₃ b), if a >= 16 and b >= 17 and b < 31; a ★₂ (♡₅ a), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 16 and b ≥ 17 and b < 31, apply ♥₃₀ to 12, then AND it with ▽₂₃ b bit by bit; otherwise apply ★₂ to a and (♡₅ a).

operators.name: ♣₃₂
operators.definition: a ♣₃₂ b = { 4 ⊻ 0, if a >= 6 and a < 19 and b >= 9 and b < 27; ♡₅ b, else }
operators.plain: If 6 ≤ a < 19 and b ≥ 9 and b < 27, XOR 4 with 0 bit by bit; otherwise apply ♡₅ to b.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ○₃₃
operators.definition: a ○₃₃ = { (◆₁₂ a) ♣₃₂ (▲₁₇ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ◆₁₂ to a, then apply ♣₃₂ to the result and (▲₁₇ a).

operators.name: ◆₃₄
operators.definition: a ◆₃₄ b = { a □₁, if a >= 0 and b >= 31; b ⇐ 6, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 0 and b ≥ 31, apply □₁ to a; otherwise shift b left by 6 bits.

operators.name: ♤₃₅
operators.definition: ♤₃₅ a = { 5, if a >= 3 and a < 10; (a ♯) ■₂₇ a, if a >= 27; (a ♣₃₂ 6) ●₁₀, else }
operators.plain: If 3 ≤ a < 10, return 5; otherwise if a ≥ 27, count the one bits of a, then apply ■₂₇ to the result and a; otherwise apply ♣₃₂ to a and 6, then apply ●₁₀ to the result.

operators.name: ◆₃₆
operators.definition: a ◆₃₆ b = { a, if a >= 28 and b >= 29; a ⇐ a, if a >= 7 and a < 28 and b >= 16 and b < 29; a ★₉ b, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 28 and b ≥ 29, return a; otherwise if 7 ≤ a < 28 and b ≥ 16 and b < 29, shift a left by a bits; otherwise compute a ★₉ b.

operators.name: ▼₃₇
operators.definition: a ▼₃₇ b = { (a □₁) ■₂₇ (▲₁₇ b) }
operators.plain: Apply □₁ to a, then apply ■₂₇ to the result and (▲₁₇ b).

operators.name: ♤₃₈
operators.definition: a ♤₃₈ b = { (♤₃₅ a) ▼₃₇ (☆₁₁ b) }
operators.plain: Apply ♤₃₅ to a, then apply ▼₃₇ to the result and (☆₁₁ b).

operators.name: ◆₃₉
operators.definition: a ◆₃₉ b = { b ♤₃₈ (a ○₃₃), if a >= 17 and a < 28 and b >= 18; ♡₅ (b ⊻ a), else }
operators.plain: If 17 ≤ a < 28 and b ≥ 18, apply ♤₃₈ to b and (a ○₃₃); otherwise XOR b with a bit by bit, then apply ♡₅ to the result.

operators.name: ■₄₀
operators.definition: ■₄₀ a = { (a ▽₄) ■₃₁ (◆₁₂ 12) }
operators.plain: Apply ▽₄ to a, then apply ■₃₁ to the result and (◆₁₂ 12).

operators.name: ○₄₁
operators.definition: ○₄₁ a = { a, if a >= 27; (♡₅ 4) ▼₁₉ (♤₂₄ a), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 27, return a; otherwise apply ♡₅ to 4, then apply ▼₁₉ to the result and (♤₂₄ a).

operators.name: ♧₄₂
operators.definition: ♧₄₂ a = { 0, if a == 0; (♧₄₂ (a ⇒ 1)) ◆₃₄ a, if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is 0; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then apply ◆₃₄ to r and a.

operators.name: ♥₄₃
operators.definition: a ♥₄₃ = { 0, if a == 0; ■₄₀ ((a ⇒ 1) ♥₄₃), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with 0. Repeat once for each right shift of a until it reaches 0 (for a from 0 to 31): apply ■₄₀ to the current value.

operators.name: ○₄₄
operators.definition: a ○₄₄ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ○₄₄ (b ⇒ 1)) ♣₆, if b > 0 and b <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat once for each right shift of b until it reaches 0 (for b from 0 to 31): apply ♣₆ to the current value.

operators.name: ●₄₅
operators.definition: ●₄₅ a = { 0, if a == 0; (●₄₅ (a ⇒ 1)) ♤₃₈ a, if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is 0; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then apply ♤₃₈ to r and a.

operators.name: ♠₄₆
operators.definition: a ♠₄₆ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♠₄₆ (b ⇒ 1)) ⊻ (a ♠₄₆ (b ⇒ 1)), if b > 0 and b <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat once for each right shift of b until it reaches 0 (for b from 0 to 31): XOR the current value with the current value bit by bit.

operators.name: ♦₄₇
operators.definition: a ♦₄₇ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♦₄₇ (b ⇒ 1)) □₁, if b > 0 and b <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat once for each right shift of b until it reaches 0 (for b from 0 to 31): apply □₁ to the current value.

operators.name: ▲₄₈
operators.definition: a ▲₄₈ b = { b, if a == 0; b ♣₃₂ ((a ⇒ 1) ▲₄₈ b), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with b. Repeat once for each right shift of a until it reaches 0 (for a from 0 to 31): replace the current value by b ♣₃₂ the current value.

operators.name: ☆₄₉
operators.definition: a ☆₄₉ b = { b, if a == 0; ((a ⇒ 1) ☆₄₉ b) ⊻ a, if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is b; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then XOR r with a bit by bit.

operators.name: ♢₅₀
operators.definition: a ♢₅₀ b = { a, if b == 0; ♠₁₈ (a ♢₅₀ (b ⇒ 1)), if b > 0 and b <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat once for each right shift of b until it reaches 0 (for b from 0 to 31): apply ♠₁₈ to the current value.

operators.name: ♥₅₁
operators.definition: a ♥₅₁ = { (a ♥₄₃) ★₉ (♡₅ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₄₃ to a, then apply ★₉ to the result and (♡₅ a).

operators.name: ♥₅₂
operators.definition: a ♥₅₂ b = { (■₄₀ b) ♢₅₀ (♧₃ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ■₄₀ to b, then apply ♢₅₀ to the result and (♧₃ a).

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ♤₅₃
operators.definition: a ♤₅₃ = { a ♢₅₀ a }
operators.plain: Compute a ♢₅₀ a.

operators.name: ●₅₄
operators.definition: a ●₅₄ b = { b ☆₄₉ (♡₅ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ☆₄₉ to b and (♡₅ a).

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ♠₅₅
operators.definition: a ♠₅₅ b = { (a ▽₄) ♦₄₇ (♤₃₅ b) }
operators.plain: Apply ▽₄ to a, then apply ♦₄₇ to the result and (♤₃₅ b).

operators.name: ♢₅₆
operators.definition: a ♢₅₆ = { (a ■₁₆) ☆₄₉ a }
operators.plain: Apply ■₁₆ to a, then apply ☆₄₉ to the result and a.

operators.name: ▲₅₇
operators.definition: a ▲₅₇ = { ☆₁₁ (a ☆₄₉ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ☆₄₉ to a and a, then apply ☆₁₁ to the result.

operators.name: ◆₅₈
operators.definition: a ◆₅₈ = { ♤₂₄ (a ●₅₄ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ●₅₄ to a and a, then apply ♤₂₄ to the result.

operators.name: ●₅₉
operators.definition: a ●₅₉ b = { a ♠₅₅ (b ♢₅₆) }
operators.plain: Apply ♠₅₅ to a and (b ♢₅₆).

operators.name: ◆₆₀
operators.definition: ◆₆₀ a = { (a ♤₅₃) ♥₅₂ (♤₂₄ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♤₅₃ to a, then apply ♥₅₂ to the result and (♤₂₄ a).

operators.name: ♥₆₁
operators.definition: a ♥₆₁ = { (■₁₅ a) ●₅₉ (0 ■₁₆) }
operators.plain: Apply ■₁₅ to a, then apply ●₅₉ to the result and (0 ■₁₆).

operators.name: ♢₆₂
operators.plain: Apply ◆₆₀ to 19, then shift it left by ♧₃ a bits.

operators.name: ☆₆₃
operators.definition: a ☆₆₃ = { (a ♥₅₂ a) ●₁₀ }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₅₂ to a and a, then apply ●₁₀ to the result.

operators.name: ●₆₄
operators.definition: ●₆₄ a = { a ○₄₄ a }
operators.plain: Compute a ○₄₄ a.

operators.name: ▼₆₅
operators.definition: a ▼₆₅ b = { a ♥₅₂ (b ▲₅₇) }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₅₂ to a and (b ▲₅₇).

operators.name: ♢₆₆
operators.definition: a ♢₆₆ b = { ♡₅ (a ⇒ b), if a >= 4 and a < 12 and b < 8; (a ♠₄₆ b) ♥₆₁, if a >= 12 and b >= 20; ▽₂₃ (b ◆₅₈), else }
operators.plain: If 4 ≤ a < 12 and b < 8, shift a right by b bits, then apply ♡₅ to the result; otherwise if a ≥ 12 and b ≥ 20, apply ♠₄₆ to a and b, then apply ♥₆₁ to the result; otherwise apply ◆₅₈ to b, then apply ▽₂₃ to the result.

operators.name: ♦₆₇
operators.definition: a ♦₆₇ b = { b ♦₂₁ b, if a < 9 and b >= 14 and b < 25; a ♥₄₃, if a < 9 and b >= 25; 0 ⇒ b, else }
operators.plain: If a < 9 and b ≥ 14 and b < 25, compute b ♦₂₁ b; otherwise if a < 9 and b ≥ 25, apply ♥₄₃ to a; otherwise shift 0 right by b bits.

operators.name: ◆₆₈
operators.definition: a ◆₆₈ = { ■₄₀ (12 ◆₅₈), if a >= 8 and a < 13; (♧₃ a) ♢₆₆ (♠₁₈ a), if a >= 0 and a < 8; (a □₁) ♦₂₁ (a □₁), else }
operators.plain: If 8 ≤ a < 13, apply ◆₅₈ to 12, then apply ■₄₀ to the result; otherwise if 0 ≤ a < 8, apply ♧₃ to a, then apply ♢₆₆ to the result and (♠₁₈ a); otherwise apply □₁ to a, then apply ♦₂₁ to the result and (itself).

operators.name: □₆₉
operators.definition: a □₆₉ b = { (a ♥₄₃) ∨ (▲₁₇ a), if a < 11 and b >= 2 and b < 22; (●₆₄ b) ♢₆₆ (b ☆₆₃), if a >= 25 and b >= 22; (♧₃ a) △₂₂ (b □₁), else }
operators.plain: If a < 11 and b ≥ 2 and b < 22, apply ♥₄₃ to a, then OR it with ▲₁₇ a bit by bit; otherwise if a ≥ 25 and b ≥ 22, apply ●₆₄ to b, then apply ♢₆₆ to the result and (b ☆₆₃); otherwise apply ♧₃ to a, then apply △₂₂ to the result and (b □₁).

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ■₇₀
operators.definition: a ■₇₀ b = { (♤₃₅ a) ●₅₉ (♤₂₄ b), if a < 23 and b < 6; a, else }
operators.plain: If a < 23 and b < 6, apply ♤₃₅ to a, then apply ●₅₉ to the result and (♤₂₄ b); otherwise return a.

operators.name: ○₇₁
operators.definition: ○₇₁ a = { a ★₂ a, if a >= 6 and a < 25; ●₄₅ 14, if a < 6; a ◆₃₉ a, else }
operators.plain: If 6 ≤ a < 25, compute a ★₂ a; otherwise if a < 6, apply ●₄₅ to 14; otherwise compute a ◆₃₉ a.

operators.name: ♡₇₂
operators.definition: a ♡₇₂ b = { ▲₁₇ (a ▲₄₈ b), if a < 12 and b >= 24; (▲₁₇ 16) ◇₁₄ (a ▽₈), if a >= 29 and b < 3; a ⇐ (◆₆₀ a), else }
operators.plain: If a < 12 and b ≥ 24, apply ▲₄₈ to a and b, then apply ▲₁₇ to the result; otherwise if a ≥ 29 and b < 3, apply ▲₁₇ to 16, then apply ◇₁₄ to the result and (a ▽₈); otherwise shift a left by ◆₆₀ a bits.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: □₇₃
operators.definition: □₇₃ a = { (2 ♥₂₉) ○₄₄ a, if a < 11; a ♢₆₆ (a ♥₆₁), else }
operators.plain: If a < 11, apply ♥₂₉ to 2, then apply ○₄₄ to the result and a; otherwise apply ♢₆₆ to a and (a ♥₆₁).

operators.name: ○₇₄
operators.definition: a ○₇₄ b = { a ⊻ b, if a >= 22 and a < 24 and b >= 11 and b < 18; ◆₆₀ 8, if a >= 31 and b >= 18; a ◆₃₆ b, else }
operators.plain: If 22 ≤ a < 24 and b ≥ 11 and b < 18, XOR a with b bit by bit; otherwise if a ≥ 31 and b ≥ 18, apply ◆₆₀ to 8; otherwise compute a ◆₃₆ b.

operators.name: ▽₇₅
operators.definition: ▽₇₅ a = { (♧₃ a) ■₇₀ a, if a < 7; a ○₇₄ a, if a >= 22 and a < 28; (7 ☆₆₃) ◆₃₉ a, else }
operators.plain: If a < 7, apply ♧₃ to a, then apply ■₇₀ to the result and a; otherwise if 22 ≤ a < 28, compute a ○₇₄ a; otherwise apply ☆₆₃ to 7, then apply ◆₃₉ to the result and a.

operators.name: △₇₆
operators.definition: a △₇₆ b = { a, if b == 0; ●₆₄ (a △₇₆ (b ⇒ 1)), if b > 0 and b <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat once for each right shift of b until it reaches 0 (for b from 0 to 31): apply ●₆₄ to the current value.

operators.name: ▽₇₇
operators.definition: ▽₇₇ a = { 0, if a == 0; (▽₇₇ (a ⇒ 1)) ▼₆₅ a, if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is 0; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then apply ▼₆₅ to r and a.

operators.name: ♡₇₈
operators.definition: a ♡₇₈ b = { 0, if b == 0; (a ♡₇₈ (b ⇒ 1)) ●₅₄ b, if b > 0 and b <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on b (for b from 0 to 31): when b = 0 the result is 0; otherwise let r be the result for b ⇒ 1, then apply ●₅₄ to r and b.

operators.name: ▲₇₉
operators.definition: a ▲₇₉ b = { b, if a == 0; ((a ⇒ 1) ▲₇₉ b) ☆₄₉ a, if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is b; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then apply ☆₄₉ to r and a.

operators.name: ▲₈₀
operators.definition: a ▲₈₀ = { 0, if a == 0; a ■₇₀ ((a ⇒ 1) ▲₈₀), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is 0; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then replace r by a ■₇₀ r.

operators.name: ○₈₁
operators.definition: a ○₈₁ b = { b, if a == 0; a ▲₄₈ ((a ⇒ 1) ○₈₁ b), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is b; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then replace r by a ▲₄₈ r.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ◆₈₂
operators.definition: a ◆₈₂ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ◆₈₂ (b ⇒ 1)) ♤₅₃, if b > 0 and b <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat once for each right shift of b until it reaches 0 (for b from 0 to 31): apply ♤₅₃ to the current value.

operators.name: ☆₈₃
operators.definition: ☆₈₃ a = { a ○₈₁ 2 }
operators.plain: Compute a ○₈₁ 2.

operators.name: ■₈₄
operators.definition: a ■₈₄ b = { (b ♥₅₁) ○₈₁ (♤₂₄ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₅₁ to b, then apply ○₈₁ to the result and (♤₂₄ a).

operators.name: ♧₈₅
operators.definition: a ♧₈₅ = { a ♡₇₈ a }
operators.plain: Compute a ♡₇₈ a.

operators.name: ♧₈₆
operators.definition: a ♧₈₆ = { a ▲₇₉ a }
operators.plain: Compute a ▲₇₉ a.

operators.name: ▲₈₇
operators.definition: a ▲₈₇ b = { (♧₃ b) ■₈₄ (a ♧₈₆) }
operators.plain: Apply ♧₃ to b, then apply ■₈₄ to the result and (a ♧₈₆).

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ♥₈₈
operators.definition: a ♥₈₈ = { a ▲₇₉ 2 }
operators.plain: Compute a ▲₇₉ 2.

operators.name: ♧₈₉
operators.definition: a ♧₈₉ b = { (b ♥₈₈) ♠₄₆ (a ♥₈₈) }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₈₈ to b, then apply ♠₄₆ to the result and (a ♥₈₈).

operators.name: ♠₉₀
operators.definition: a ♠₉₀ b = { (b ♥₈₈) ◆₃₉ a }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₈₈ to b, then apply ◆₃₉ to the result and a.

operators.name: ♢₉₁
operators.definition: a ♢₉₁ = { (a ♧₈₆) ○₄₄ (▽₇₅ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♧₈₆ to a, then apply ○₄₄ to the result and (▽₇₅ a).

operators.name: ♢₉₂
operators.definition: a ♢₉₂ b = { (b ♦₂₁ a) ♥₈₈ }
operators.plain: Apply ♦₂₁ to b and a, then apply ♥₈₈ to the result.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order and negation

operators.name: ◇₉₃
operators.definition: a ◇₉₃ = { ▽₂₃ (a ♡₇₈ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♡₇₈ to a and a, then apply ▽₂₃ to the result.

operators.name: ♥₉₄
operators.definition: ♥₉₄ a = { a ♢₉₂ (▽₇₇ 4), if a < 11; a, else }
operators.plain: If a < 11, apply ♢₉₂ to a and (▽₇₇ 4); otherwise return a.

operators.name: ♦₉₅
operators.definition: a ♦₉₅ b = { a ◆₃₆ b, if a >= 20 and b >= 25; b ♧₈₆, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 20 and b ≥ 25, compute a ◆₃₆ b; otherwise apply ♧₈₆ to b.

operators.name: ♤₉₆
operators.definition: a ♤₉₆ b = { ■₄₀ a, if a >= 17 and b >= 13; b ○₈₁ b, if a >= 6 and a < 17 and b >= 13; a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 17 and b ≥ 13, apply ■₄₀ to a; otherwise if 6 ≤ a < 17 and b ≥ 13, compute b ○₈₁ b; otherwise return a.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order and negation

operators.name: ♥₉₇
operators.definition: a ♥₉₇ b = { (▽₇₅ 27) ♦₆₇ (0 ♧₈₆), if a >= 1 and a < 3 and b >= 11; b ◆₃₆ (a ♥₅₁), else }
operators.plain: If 1 ≤ a < 3 and b ≥ 11, apply ▽₇₅ to 27, then apply ♦₆₇ to the result and (0 ♧₈₆); otherwise apply ◆₃₆ to b and (a ♥₅₁).

operators.name: △₉₈
operators.definition: a △₉₈ = { a, if a >= 29; ♥₉₄ 26, if a < 0; a ▲₈₇ a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 29, return a; otherwise if a < 0, apply ♥₉₄ to 26; otherwise compute a ▲₈₇ a.

operators.name: □₉₉
operators.definition: a □₉₉ = { a ▲₈₀, if a >= 4 and a < 28; ▲₁₇ a, else }
operators.plain: If 4 ≤ a < 28, apply ▲₈₀ to a; otherwise apply ▲₁₇ to a.

operators.name: ■₁₀₀
operators.definition: ■₁₀₀ a = { ☆₁₁ (a ⇐ a), if a >= 30; a, if a < 10; (▽₂₃ 7) ♥₉₇ (◆₁₂ 4), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 30, shift a left by a bits, then apply ☆₁₁ to the result; otherwise if a < 10, return a; otherwise apply ▽₂₃ to 7, then apply ♥₉₇ to the result and (◆₁₂ 4).
